Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking What can you possibly say new about Monopoly, the world's favorite property trading game, that hasn't already been said for decades since it's introduction by Parker Brothers in 1935? No matter what new version of Monopoly comes out, it's always so much fun to play with family and friends.

In the sixties, we always had one major problem when the entire family sat down to a long night of playing Monopoly, and that was, we always ran out of money if the game went on long enough. There used to be an office store named Burrows that sold extra Monopoly money and buying an extra packet or two was the only solution to our money shortage.

Now with this new version of Monopoly With Electronic Banking, you'll never run out of money, because there isn't any. The game comes with the standard board, dice, houses, hotels, Title Deed cards, Chance and Community Chest cards, 6 tokens and 6 bank cards that slide through an electronic banking unit which keeps track of your cash on your card. The electronic unit takes 2 AAA batteries (Not Included) and can store millions of dollars on each player's bank card.

It actually takes just as long to type in the money you accumulate on each player's card, as it does to hand count the cash to the players, so don't think this electronic unit is a time saver. We actually found when playing with 6 players, that it saved time to have a separate banker. This electronic banking version of Monopoly may not be faster than the cash version, but it's every bit as fun and that's saying a lot for a game that's been rated number one for over 75 years!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking

NERF Infinus N-Strike Elite Toy Motorized Blaster with Speed-Load Technology Holiday gift for my 6 year old -- and a waste of money. He got around 30 minutes of joy, because when it works it's kinda-sorta cool. But it takes too long to start firing, especially in the heat of battle, and it lacks enough power to send the darts very far.

The big problem is that this thing constantly jams, especially if the batteries start getting low. And this thing chews through batteries like few toys I've seen before. The jams are super frustrating, often tricky to resolve without doing any damage the gun or ruining the dart.

I've figured out through trial and error that this gun is very sensitive to dart width. I discovered quite by accident that some Nerf darts, even with the same color tips, have slightly different widths than some others. There are letter codes on the side of the dart that seem to correspond to which ones work better. The "J" ones we have seem to be okay, the "A" ones not so much. The difference is subtle, but you can tell when loading some of the manual guns, as some darts will offer more resistance. The tolerance is not an issue with those guns, but it's a huge problem with this one, as the wider darts consistently jam. Of course we don't have all of our darts sorted by 1mm width differences or tiny letters printed on the side of the tips, so every time my child wants to play with this gun we have to go through and check each dart one at a time to increase the odds that we'll have a good experience. That's ridiculous.

I think we paid around $50 for this. I think it's worth around $5. Not recommended at all.
text_fidelity_b: NERF Infinus N-Strike Elite Toy Motorized Blaster with Speed-Load Technology

text_fidelity_a:
So Slime DIY - Mini Slime Caddy Our library has monthly slime making labs that my children enjoy. It's created a greater interest in the world of slime for them and it's something fun for us to enjoy when boredom strikes, especially in the late evening/night hours. This kit was enjoyed by all of us. It comes with a little caddy(and a removeable tray) to hold the supplies. Inside, there are two containers for making the slime, stickers for decorating the containers, 4 packs of slime powder, 4 packs of decoration(glitter and small shapes), and 2 little toys(ours isn't what's shown...star and cloud here). To make the slime, all the maker has to do is add the slime powder and any glitter/shapes they want, then fill to the line with water, put the top on, *hold* it on well, and then shake it until it's the right consistency. We had to shake longer than the directions said, but it still doesn't take long and it's super easy.

Just to note, the glitter still gets everywhere. It doesn't stick to the slime like I thought it would. While playing with the slime, it came off on our hands a great deal. I found glitter everywhere afterwards, despite us trying to be careful with it. It was on us, the table, the floor, the couches. My husband wasn't even here when we made it, nor did he play with it, but he even ended up with glitter on his face the next day. So, keep that in mind if you dislike glitter as much as I do. Too, my children didn't like the shapes in the slime, saying it poked their hands. It comes off the slime, too. Otherwise, we've enjoyed it!
text_fidelity_b: So Slime DIY - Mini Slime Caddy

text_fidelity_a: Backyard Discovery Sweetwater All Cedar White Modern Outdoor Wooden Playhouse, Cottage, Sink, Stove, Windows, Kitchen with Pot and Pans and Utensils, Flowerpot Holders, Working Doorbell, Ages 2-6 We've had this playhouse for a couple of months and it still looks brand new - despite the Iowa sun, our extreme heat and rain and freezes.  When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!

text_fidelity_a:
Goopow Kids Camera Toys for 3-8 Year Old Girls,Children Digital Video Camcorder Camera with Unicorn Soft Silicone Cover, Best Christmas Birthday Festival Gift for Kids - 32G SD Card Included [[VIDEOID:fd8e8c92f2d5416e2ee661d5841a9c4c]] This is definitely a fantastic camera for younger kids. It has a LOT of really great features that will keep this in my son's road-trip arsenal. Picture quality is what you SHOULD expect for this price range. They're fairly grainy in low light, and they aren't exactly cutting edge...but this is FOR YOUNGER KIDS!

Pros:
RUGGED - The camera itself is already rubberized and very thick. THEN it has a thick rubber cover. This is going to hold up against anything my youngest could possibly do to it.
Frames - There are different fun frames and "accessories" to overlay on the photos. Think of this as a kid's version of SnapChat. It's really pretty fun.
Games - There are three included GAMES, and they work surprisingly well for being on a camera. There's Tetris (awesome), Snaker (a Snake clone), and a block moving game. Tetris is fantastic.
Video - Yeah...This shoots video. The camera has a built in mic, too. My son is going to love this...My poor dogs.
MicroSD - Comes bundled with a 32GB MicroSD card. NICE. It also has a USB reader for easy transfer to the computer. Very NICE.
Battery - Rechargeable battery built in. Charges with micro USB cable. Seems to have great battery life compared to other kid's cameras, too. I took pictures over and over...screen stays on. I did pre-view on camera of the different pictures..Took a few videos. One was about five minutes, but the rest were short clips. Battery still going strong.

Cons:
Picture/Video Quality - Fairly standard for a camera in this price range meant for kids. This isn't really a con, as I knew what to expect. I'm including this so people don't think they're getting their kid a professional camera. It's not really a bad thing for me.

Overall, this is a great value. I got this for a six year old, and he is going to be in love with it. It does everything a kid cares about: 1. Looks cool. 2. Takes pictures. 3. Takes Video. 4. Plays Games. Every picture and video is going to be amazing to him. Thinking of it like that...This camera is going to be his favorite Christmas gift this year.
text_fidelity_b: Goopow Kids Camera Toys for 3-8 Year Old Girls,Children Digital Video Camcorder Camera with Unicorn Soft Silicone Cover, Best Christmas Birthday Festival Gift for Kids - 32G SD Card Included

text_fidelity_a:
Zynga Draw Something Game For years now app makers have been taking your favorite childhood games and turning them into apps. Welp, Hasbro has had enough of that and has decided to turn the tables on them. Now your favorite adulthood apps have been turned into good old fashioned board games. Take that app designers!

No, really. The Draw Something app that is so popular amongst your co-workers, it is now a board game. Packaged in a giant pencil box (odd as the writing utensils it arrives with are crayons) you get enough of what you need for up to four people to play (coin tracker clips, crayons, draw stations, and paper pads) in addition to that you get 180 word cards and a game guide.

Appropriate for the whole family (unless you have some of THOSE types of adults -- you know the ones). Great for people who want to practice their drawing skills, encourage the kiddies to be creative, or just get the family away from the electronics (what better way to trick them into a family fun night than by using a board game of their favorite app?).

The official site doesn't list replacement parts for sale which is no big deal for crayons but could be for the game pads so if you're a prolific arteest you'll have to find the right sized paper pads or make your own.
text_fidelity_b: Zynga Draw Something Game

The concept of the game is simple and easy to learn (making sequences, and the joker faces can be anything you need like a wild card). I’m not sure what happened to our family’s original old set, so I’m thrilled to have a new version for our game closet.

The battery for the copter charged quickly. The batteries for the controls come with, but you'll need a tiny screwdriver to get them in.

Flying inside is easier than outside, though completely not recommended. The copter is so light, it is susceptible to the gentlest wind. The controls are very hair-sensitive, making it difficult to steer with any accuracy. As such, fly in a large field. Otherwise, expect it stuck in a tree, land on a roof, or be busted up on the street.

Extra blades are included. After a few crashes, I can see they'll be necessary. I don't expect it to be durable with any extended use.

I'm giving it three stars because it does work as advertised. Overall, however, I'm unimpressed.

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining My children have enjoyed various kinds of dig kits in the past, so they were excited for this one, too. My 5 year old got this one, and he liked it pretty well.

On my side, though, this particular kit wasn't one of my favorites. The kit comes with a hammer, but that thing was absolutely useless! My child was frustrated with it, so I gave it a try. Useless! The description tells you that you'll get a pair of goggles, but you don't. There's no goggles in this kit, but the instructions recommend that your child wear a pair. Also, I dislike that all of the rocks were clumped in one little spot in ours, and that happen to be right where my child started digging. He got them all dug out very quickly, but still had a great deal of clay to dig through. Discovering "treasures" slowly(at least more slowly than this one) is the whole fun of these things.

Like all dig kits, this one is messy. We've found shallow pie pans to be the best holders. The sides aren't too tall, so it won't hurt your child's arms. It also keeps the mess inside the pan. For the kits that are harder to dig, it makes it super easy to move the dig until your child wants to work on it again. This particular dig is on the softer side, though not the softest we've ever done. Really, it's just right in that area, for our tastes. It's not so hard that it's frustrating, but not so soft that the dig ends in a few minutes(or it wouldn't have if ours had the gems spaced out better).

Overall, if your child enjoys rocks(or gems), this is a decent choice. There are better options, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining

Earthtiles Wooden Magnetic Tiles by Big Future Toys - 100 Piece Set | Montessori Toys | Sensory Toys | Wooden Magnetic Blocks | STEM Building Toys | Wooden Blocks for Toddlers| Toddler Toys Age 3+ [[VIDEOID:2ed5b4ed724fe0fbfda0f1674e634e3d]] Good set of magnetic building shapes with a few thoughts. My kiddo was at a play-date recently, and the friend had a plastic set that the kids really enjoyed playing with. I saw these for review and thought they’d be a great addition to our play area at home. One thing I noticed right from the start is that they sound like baby rattles—you can really hear the magnets moving around inside as you move them. I didn’t notice this type of noise with the plastic ones at the play-date, so just something to keep in mind.

The wood is very smooth and each piece is lightweight. They appear to be durable as I don’t notice any bend if I put pressure on one of the pieces, but they also seem thin at the same time. I’m a little concerned that if someone steps on these by mistake, one of them could crack in half and expose little magnets everywhere. Up until this point, I’ve avoided a lot of toys with magnets, so I’m just going to have to be selective about when we play with these so I can really supervise how they’re being used.

Like magnets naturally do, sometimes the sides won’t link correctly if the positive and negative sides are connected right, so this is a normal learning curve for kids. Otherwise, they stand together very well and there’s plenty of pieces and shapes to build some neat things. These are very nice overall, and if you prefer wooden toys, these are a very good option.
text_fidelity_b: Earthtiles Wooden Magnetic Tiles by Big Future Toys - 100 Piece Set | Montessori Toys | Sensory Toys | Wooden Magnetic Blocks | STEM Building Toys | Wooden Blocks for Toddlers| Toddler Toys Age 3+

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil The letters in this book aren't done in order. If you're wanting this book to teach letters, that might be important to know. I've chosen to teach in order, and am working on that with my two oldest. (I know some teach letters out of order, which is great, too) Either way, with this book they're learning letters. Plus, there's an alphabet chart on the last page that does put the letters in the correct order. It seems as though the letters in this book are introduced according to how easy they are to write(straight lines, curves, etc). So, as your child goes along, the letters get harder and harder to write.

Also, both uppercase and lowercase letters are included in this book.

Each page in the book has a little practice sheet. These sheets are super sensitive to pressure. Any pressure at all from any source, and a "pencil" mark will show up where you've written. Once you've used these sheets, they are useless. (You can't erase) You are provided with an extra set of sheets, and given the warning to NOT stack and to separate them before writing. When your little one is done with the sheets, they can be easily torn out, and the book will work perfectly fine without them. Your child can still practice "writing" letters just using the book.

Since music is an important part of this book's story, I enjoyed that added lesson for my little ones. There's even a piano included that can be played, which makes me like this book even more.

Overall, this is a wonderful tool to have for learning! I'm looking forward to adding the numbers book to our library soon!
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended I'm not quite the telescope connoisseur, though I'm quite well versed in optics (avid photographer), and I've discovered there's a bit of a gulf between the "wouldn't it be nice to have a telescope" and those sold to diehard astronomers. This one falls into the former category, and as such I"m not really comparing this to higher end models.

In the lower end realm, I still expect clear optics, no noticeable optical defects, and a stable base. This one checks those boxes. The optics look clean and clear to the naked eye, though lab testing would show where higher end models excel, and it's not the brightest lens (all lenses lose some light due to transmission loss in lens materials and dispersal), but it met my expectations. The tripod is well built enough for this model telescope, but it's no remarkable. As it's geared towards budding astronomers, especially youngsters, the included guide and list of projects to get you going is definitely a strength.

4 stars due to no faults of it's own, though it's not that remarkable either. Recommended, though may want to consider other models.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

The cars race down and then we do it all over again! I do wish it had some minimal sound effects, like a "beep" button, or some rumble bumps on the track...something fun like that.

If you find yourself having a hard time with them, make sure they are in the right spot, as they went on easily once they were in the correct position. Barbie Printastic Hair Doll Barbie Hair Tattoos Doll has fast become a favorite doll in our household. The girls in our family have always loved styling Barbie doll's hair as much as they love coordinating her wardrobe and styling her home. The doll itself is simply beautiful with her hip length blonde hair, mod print mini dress and high heels.

Barbie also comes with a styling salon chair, 13 tattoo design strips, a flat iron, comb, hair clip, 2 hair bands, 3 barrettes and a water bottle. To make Barbie's hair decorated with the colorful tattoo designs, you comb out her hair smooth, clip one of the 13 tattoo designs to her hair, spray it with water and then swipe it with the flat iron. The tattoo ink is non staining- thank goodness, as sometimes they get left on a table after using.

We quickly found that experimenting with the hair amount and smoothness, the water being cold, warm or hot and the pressure and speed we use with the flat iron do affect the way the tattoos come out on Barbie's hair. We also noticed that some tattoos come out way better than others, no matter what you do. We found that really flat combed hair, warm water and pulling the flat iron hard and slowly gave some great results on some of the tattoo patterns. Others just looked like color blobs.

This all really didn't even seem to matter, as the girls love this doll and especially when the tattoos came out looking pretty good in her hair. When they didn't look good, the tattoos just washed out in a minute. For the tattoos that didn't turn out on Barbie, the girls ended up putting the tattoos on themselves as bracelets on their wrists or ankles. They had fun no matter if the tattoos came out good or bad looking in Barbie's hair, so this Barbie Hair Tattoos is still worth 4 Stars, even though you have to experiment to get some of the tattoos to look great.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Printastic Hair Doll
